18: KHLESTAKOV [escorting him]. Not at all. What you told me is all very funny. Call again, please. I like that sort of thing very much. [Turns back and reopens the door, calling.] I say, there! What is your——I keep forgetting. What is your first name and your patronymic?
16: ARTEMY. I don't venture to disturb you any longer with my presence and rob you of your time dedicated to the performance of your sacred duties—-[Bows and makes to go.]
12: ARTEMY. Nikolay, Ivan, Yelizaveta, Marya and Perepetuya.
11: KHLESTAKOV. Yes, yes, what are their names?
10: KHLESTAKOV. You don't say! Grown up! And how are they—how are they—a—a? ARTEMY. You mean that you deign to ask what their names are?
9: ARTEMY. Of course. Five. Two are already grown up.
8: ARTEMY. Zemlianika. KHLESTAKOV. Oh, yes, Zemlianika. Tell me, Mr. Zemlianika, have you any children?
6: KHLESTAKOV. Very well, why not? I should like it very much. I like to kill the weary hours reading something amusing, you know. What is your name? I keep forgetting.
4: ARTEMY. Then take the School Inspector here. I don't know how the government could have entrusted him with such an office. He's worse than a Jacobin freethinker, and he instils such pernicious ideas into the minds of the young that I can hardly describe it. Hadn't I better put it all down on paper, if you so order?
3: KHLESTAKOV. You don't say so. I never imagined it.
2: KHLESTAKOV. I admit, my weakness is a good cuisine.—Tell me, please, won't you—it seems to me you were a little shorter yesterday, weren't you?
0: ARTEMY. I am glad to do all I can in behalf of my country.
